workflow_plan.goal: Calculate mean elevation for the State College census tracts using elevation data at 30-meter resolution or finer.

workflow_steps.title: Retrieve State College census tracts
workflow_steps.purpose: Obtain census tract polygons covering the State College area for zonal elevation statistics.
workflow_steps.instructions: Retrieve the highest-ranked census tract polygon dataset covering the State College boundary. Treat the result as a candidate and retain its runtime metadata for QC; do not assume field names or analytical fitness before inspection.

workflow_steps.title: Constrain census tracts to State College
workflow_steps.purpose: Use the supplied State College boundary to retain the census tract portions relevant to the requested area.
workflow_steps.instructions: Clip the retrieved census tract layer to the supplied State College boundary. Preserve the census tract identifier attributes and do not infer or rename schema fields.

workflow_steps.title: Calculate mean elevation by census tract
workflow_steps.purpose: Compute the mean elevation for each State College census tract using the supplied DEM at 30-meter resolution.
workflow_steps.instructions: Compute mean zonal elevation for the state_college_census_tracts polygons using input_2 as the analytical raster. Ground the tract identifier field and any required output field names from runtime schema inspection; do not guess field names. input_1 is an alternate lower-resolution DEM and must not be selected for the requested 30-meter-or-finer analysis.

requirements.scope: The retrieved census tract candidate must cover the supplied State College boundary and provide the census tracts needed for the requested area.
The retrieved census tract layer and input_3 must have compatible CRSs before clipping.
The census tract and State College boundary geometries used for clipping must be valid and non-empty.
The analytical elevation raster must have pixel resolution no coarser than 30 meters.
The analytical raster and clipped census tract polygons must have compatible CRSs for zonal statistics.
The clipped census tract polygons used for zonal statistics must be valid and non-empty.
The clipped census tract layer must contain a field that uniquely identifies each tract so the output means can be attributed to individual census tracts.
